# Unify global Admin sidenav with collapsible domains and no-group scope

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-08-05
- **Requested by**: Ian Starnes

## Description

Make the standalone admin portal use one clean, global Admin sidenav modeled on the proven web-mojo Sidebar behavior. Admin is never group-scoped. Group navigation remains a separate capability for product portals, where active-group context selects project-defined menus.

## Context

The current base portal splits global destinations between a Main menu and an AdminSections menu, renders every AdminSection child continuously, and mounts the active-group switcher/provider app-wide. With nineteen admin domains planned, the navigation will become overloaded and the visible group context incorrectly suggests that global admin work is group-scoped. The previous `web-mojo/src/core/views/navigation/Sidebar.js` used collapsible submenus, active-branch expansion, and an optional icon rail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The standalone base admin exposes Dashboard, Users, Groups, API keys, and every registered AdminSection through one global Admin menu.
- [ ] Admin destinations are grouped into clean collapsible domain categories; only one category is open normally and the active route's category opens automatically.
- [ ] The Admin sidebar provides quick navigation search and can collapse to an icon rail with accessible labels/tooltips.
- [ ] The standalone Admin shell does not render a group switcher, does not provide member-derived permission context, and removes/ignores a stale `?group=` query parameter without forgetting a product portal's stored group.
- [ ] Package menu contracts retain project-defined group menus selected by `group.kind`; this change does not remove group navigation from portal-mojo consumers.
- [ ] Existing AdminSection route and permission gates remain fail-closed and root/embedded dual mounts remain supported.
- [ ] Light/dark browser verification covers accordion behavior, active branches, search, rail collapse, direct admin routes, and clean console output.
- [ ] Root typecheck and production builds for portal and showcase pass.

## Investigation

- **What exists**: `packages/portal-mojo/src/ui/menu-registry.ts` derives the active menu from route/group/user; `SidebarNav.tsx` renders children permanently; `apps/portal/src/menus.ts` registers separate Main, Group, and Admin menus; `apps/portal/src/components/Sidebar.tsx` always renders GroupSwitcher; `apps/portal/src/main.tsx` mounts GroupProvider over the standalone app.
- **What changes**: enrich menu data with stable ids/scope and collapsible categories, group AdminSection contributions by operator domain, merge the base app into one Admin menu, and remove active-group chrome/context from the standalone admin.
- **Constraints**: preserve `sys.*` global permission gates, route-derived menu selection, hash-router URLs, dual-mount AdminSections, both themes, and compatibility for custom group-kind menus.
- **Related files**: `web-mojo/src/core/views/navigation/Sidebar.js`; `packages/portal-mojo/src/ui/menu-registry.ts`; `packages/portal-mojo/src/ui/SidebarNav.tsx`; `packages/portal-mojo/src/admin/index.ts`; `apps/portal/src/menus.ts`; `apps/portal/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`; `apps/portal/src/App.tsx`; `apps/portal/src/main.tsx`; `apps/portal/src/theme.css`; package docs and `PLAN.md`.
- **Out of scope**: building unfinished admin domains, changing backend endpoints, or redesigning individual admin pages.

## Plan

### Objective

Make the standalone base portal a strictly global Admin experience: one route-derived menu, organized into accessible accordion categories with search and an optional icon rail. Preserve portal-mojo's group-kind menu registry for product portals, but remove group state, member permissions, and group chrome from the standalone admin app.

### Implementation

1. **Extend the package menu contract without breaking existing consumers** (`packages/portal-mojo/src/ui/menu-registry.ts`).
   - Add stable optional `MenuItem.id` values for non-route parents, opt-in `MenuConfig.presentation: 'accordion'`, and an optional `MenuConfig.scope` discriminator (`admin`, `group`, `account`, or `global`; infer `group` from `groupKind` when omitted). Existing menus default to today's static presentation.
   - Add `MenuItem.permissionClauses`, evaluated as AND across clauses and ANY within each clause, while preserving the existing `permissions` ANY-of field. Admin contributions use clauses to retain section-gate AND route-gate semantics after category flattening.
   - Preserve the existing route/permission/group-kind resolution order and exports. Scope is descriptive shell metadata, not a new authorization mechanism.
   - Add small pure helpers for descendant-route matching and visible-tree filtering so the renderer can determine active branches without duplicating permission logic.

2. **Restore collapsible navigation behavior in React** (`packages/portal-mojo/src/ui/SidebarNav.tsx`).
   - Render a pure parent with children as an accessible disclosure button (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) instead of an always-open side label.
   - Keep a single root category open during normal browsing; automatically open the visible category containing the active route. A user may close/reopen it until navigation changes.
   - Add a controlled internal quick-filter with an explicit label, live result count/no-results status, and Escape-to-clear: matching descendants remain under their category and all matching categories expose results while search is active; clearing search restores the active accordion branch.
   - Support `collapsed` and `onRequestExpand` props. In icon-rail mode render only root destinations/categories with `aria-label` plus a real CSS hover/focus tooltip; clicking/activating a category expands the rail and opens it.
   - Keep dividers, badges, permission filtering, route matching, and group-kind compatibility intact.

3. **Give AdminSection contributions operator-domain categories** (`packages/portal-mojo/src/admin/index.ts` and each shipped section index).
   - Add an optional typed navigation group to `AdminSection`: Identity & Access, Security, Observability, Operations, Infrastructure, Communications, or Assistant. External/legacy sections with no group land deterministically under Other, preserving source compatibility.
   - Assign Credentials → Identity & Access, Monitoring → Observability, Settings → Operations, and Bouncer → Security.
   - Change `adminSectionsMenu()` to group visible section destinations into stable category parents while retaining route gates, section gates, mount-relative paths, index redirects, and embedded `/system` support. Flattened children carry conjunctive permission clauses so section AND route gates survive. Sections with multiple labeled routes contribute those routes directly; a single/index-only section contributes its section landing.
   - Fix the existing dual-mount collision: for root sections (`basePath: ''`) emit exactly one mount landing (for example `/system`) that selects the first route visible under both gates, instead of one duplicate landing per root section. Non-root section landings remain section-local.

4. **Build one standalone Admin menu** (`apps/portal/src/menus.ts`).
   - Replace separate `main`, fallback `group`, and `admin-sections` registrations with one `scope: 'admin'` menu.
   - Seed Overview with Dashboard and Identity & Access with Users, Groups, and personal API Keys, then merge the categorized `ADMIN_SECTIONS` contributions by stable category id.
   - Keep the package registry's group-menu feature untouched; product portals continue registering their own `groupKind` menus outside this standalone app.

5. **Make the standalone shell truly no-group** (`apps/portal/src/main.tsx`, `apps/portal/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`, `apps/portal/src/App.tsx`).
   - Remove `GroupProvider`, GroupSwitcher, the fallback group menu, and the standalone `/group` overview route from the base admin artifact. Admin components already use optional context and system-pinned gates.
   - On boot, remove a stale real-search `group` parameter with `history.replaceState` while leaving `active_group_id` storage untouched, so a separate product portal can restore its group.
   - Own the icon-rail state in `App`, persist it under an app-specific key, and pass it to the shell/sidebar renderer.

6. **Add the visual contract** (`apps/portal/src/theme.css`).
   - Add accordion parent/arrow/submenu, navigation search, collapse toggle, and 64px rail styles using existing tokens in both themes.
   - Keep the sidebar body independently scrollable and the footer pinned. Honor reduced motion and preserve focus-visible outlines.
   - Do not copy Bootstrap collapse machinery; use React state and semantic buttons.

7. **Update package documentation and plan history** (`packages/portal-mojo/docs/menus-and-access.md`, `packages/portal-mojo/README.md`, `PLAN.md`).
   - Document menu scopes, stable category ids, accordion/search/rail behavior, AdminSection navigation groups, and the standalone-admin no-group rule.
   - Clarify that product portals own GroupProvider/GroupSwitcher and group-kind menus; embedded Admin still uses system-pinned routes under its mount.
   - Record the navigation correction before further Admin domains land.

### Design decisions

- **One Admin menu, not a mode switch inside the base app**: the standalone artifact is itself the global back office. Group mode belongs to consuming product portals, so retaining a group test route in Admin would preserve the misleading model Ian rejected.
- **Remove GroupProvider rather than merely hide GroupSwitcher**: hiding chrome would still fetch an active member and make non-`sys.` permission mistakes possible. Absence of context makes the boundary structural; existing system-pinned gates remain the first line of defense.
- **Preserve stored group, strip only the Admin URL parameter**: a separate product portal may legitimately remember the last group. Admin must not advertise or deep-link it, but should not erase unrelated product state.
- **Categorize in `AdminSection`, render in the generic registry**: future domains declare where they belong once and work in standalone or embedded mounts. The shell does not hard-code every contributed route. The field is optional for external sections, with an Other fallback.
- **One-open accordion with search override**: normal navigation stays compact; search can expose multiple matching categories because hiding results behind accordion state defeats filtering.
- **Accordion is opt-in per menu**: the standalone Admin requests it explicitly. Existing route-less parents in custom group menus retain their current static rendering unless a consumer opts in.
- **Icon rail is app shell state**: the package renderer supports it, but layout width and persistence belong to the consuming app.

### Edge cases and error handling

- A category whose children are all permission-denied is pruned, including its divider/parent.
- Direct navigation to a child opens its category even after a different category was manually opened.
- Empty search results announce a visible no-results message; search never changes routes or permissions.
- Collapsing while search is active hides the field/results but retains the query until expansion; the user can clear it after expanding.
- Missing `MenuItem.id` falls back to a deterministic route/label-derived key for compatibility, with stable ids used by the built-in Admin menu.
- A denied direct route still fails in `adminSectionRoutes()` before its component fetches; menu restructuring does not weaken route guards.
- A flattened menu child must pass every `permissionClauses` entry. Having only the section grant or only the route grant is insufficient.
- Embedded mounts receive one root landing across all root sections, so a logs-only operator is not intercepted by a credentials-owned duplicate `/system` route.
- Removing `?group=` preserves other real-search parameters and the hash route.

### Testing

- Establish and close with `npm run typecheck`.
- Run `npm run build -w portal` and `npm run build -w showcase` after the final source/doc changes.
- Browser-test the mock portal from a stale `/?group=1#/` URL: confirm the parameter is removed, no group switcher appears, mock call counts contain no active-group or member request, and the same unified Admin menu is present on Dashboard and direct Admin routes.
- In both light and dark themes verify: only the active category opens; opening another closes it; direct child navigation reopens the correct category; search is labeled, finds nested destinations, announces result/no-result state, and clears with Escape; icon rail collapses/expands with keyboard-accessible labels and focus/hover tooltips; System routes remain permission-gated; console has no warnings/errors.
- Exercise `adminSectionRoutes()`/`adminSectionsMenu()` with a temporary external-style section whose section and route permissions differ and with two root sections under `/system`; verify menu visibility requires both grants and only one embedded mount landing is produced. Do this as a focused development assertion or small checked fixture without introducing a new test framework.

### Documentation

- Update the package menu/access reference and package export summary.
- Update `PLAN.md` with the global Admin versus group-project navigation decision and Maestro item/commit evidence.

### Challenge

- **Amended — flattened permissions could weaken the menu gate.** The challenger correctly showed that `MenuItem.permissions` is ANY-only while `AdminRoute.permissions` is additional to the section gate. The plan now adds conjunctive permission clauses and explicitly verifies section-only, route-only, both, and neither behavior.
- **Amended — embedded root sections already collide at `/system`.** Credentials and Monitoring both use `basePath: ''`, so the current helper can emit duplicate mount landings. The plan now emits one cross-section mount landing and verifies a logs-only operator path.
- **Amended — global accordion behavior and required categories would break consumers.** Navigation groups are now optional with an Other fallback, and accordion presentation is opt-in on the standalone Admin menu; existing custom/group menus keep static parents by default.
- **Amended — native titles and visual checks are not sufficient accessibility evidence.** The plan now requires labeled search, live results, Escape clearing, unique disclosure relationships, keyboard activation, and real hover/focus rail tooltips.
- **Rebutted — removing GroupProvider from the standalone Admin breaks shipped pages.** Repository search shows `useActiveGroup()` only in the GroupSwitcher/GroupOverview pair being removed. Admin pages use optional `GroupContext` reads and system-pinned gates. Verification is strengthened to prove no group/member calls; product consumers retain GroupProvider and group-kind menus.
